direction_as_read: positive for venous symptoms in small diosmin trials at 450 and 600 mg, none placebo controlled with a named primary outcome; class-level Cochrane review finds a slight oedema benefit and little or no change in quality of life
summary: One label prints DiosVein Diosmin EP 900 mg; two print Diosmin 450 mg plus Micronized Purified Flavonoid Fraction 500 mg. A placebo RCT of a branded bioavailable diosmin at 450 mg daily (33808784, 72 completers) reports better pain and venous scores but names no primary outcome. Trials with a named primary outcome have no placebo: 600 mg noninferior to micronized diosmin plus hesperidin (32206351), 1.8 g/day after knee replacement (38109425), and 600 mg added to rivaroxaban after DVT (32348101). The stored Cochrane review (33141449) pools phlebotonics as a class and gives no diosmin result in its abstract.
question_for_clinician: Recommend no credit from this review. 32206351 meets rule 2 on its face (diosmin alone, 600 mg, chronic venous disease, primary VAS noninferior) but has no placebo arm and labels print 450 and 900 mg. 33808784 matches the 450 mg row and has placebo, but it names no primary outcome and is a branded preparation. Do these support a venous symptom purpose for the rows printed?

population.description: Patients with chronic venous disease, CEAP C2-C4; 72 completed.

outcomes.name: Leg edema decreased in the active group from week 4 (p < 0.001)
VAS pain improved compared with placebo at end of treatment (p < 0.05)
Global Index Score and Venous Clinical Severity Score improved in the active group at week 8 (p < 0.001)

limitations: A branded bioavailable diosmin; randomized number not printed, only completers. Edema, GIS and VCSS wording does not state a between-group comparison.

read_not_used.33141449: Cochrane review of phlebotonics as a class, 56 RCTs, 11 on hidrosmine and diosmine; abstract gives no diosmin-specific result and says findings for specific groups are limited.
read_not_used.34556990: State-of-the-art review of three trials of diosmin 600 mg vs MPFF 1000 mg; not a meta-analysis and argues for the 600 mg dose.

stop_or_hold: MPFF is a diosmin and hesperidin mixture, and on the Youthful Legs labels both rows carry canonical diosmin; MPFF placebo trials were not read, so this packet says nothing about MPFF alone. Fields can't compare 'EP' diosmin 900 mg with a branded bioavailable 450 mg or nonmicronized 600 mg.
